## QUESTION 1

1. __Repeat the classification exercise using 2 different algorithms/models. Explain the differences between the 3 models__ (your original one, and the 2 new ones for this task).

When using a RandomForestClassifier, a GaussianNB, and SVC models, each model came back with different accuracies.

The RandomForestClassifier was the highest performer with an accuracy over 90%.

The GaussianNB model was the 2nd best having an accuracy of around 77%

The SVC model ended up being the worst of the three with an accuracy of around 72%

```{python}
 # Include and execute your code here
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
from sklearn.svm import SVC

homes = pl.read_csv("dwellings_ml.csv")


predictors = ["stories", "numbaths", "livearea", "basement", "quality_C", "gartype_Att"]

features = homes.select(predictors).to_numpy()
targets = homes["before1980"].to_numpy()

train_data, test_data, train_targets, test_targets = train_test_split(features, targets, test_size = .3)

 # Uses the same RandomForestClassifier model as before on the data.
 # Then calculates the accuracy, precision, and recall of the model.

RFC_classifier = RandomForestClassifier()

RFC_classifier.fit(train_data, train_targets)

RFC_targets_predicted = RFC_classifier.predict(test_data)

RFC_accuracy = metrics.accuracy_score(test_targets, RFC_targets_predicted)

 # Uses the GaussianNB model on the same data.
 # Then calculates the accuracy, precision, and recall of the model.

GNB_classifier = GaussianNB()

GNB_classifier.fit(train_data, train_targets)

GNB_targets_predicted = GNB_classifier.predict(test_data)

GNB_accuracy = metrics.accuracy_score(test_targets, GNB_targets_predicted)

 # Uses the SVC model on the same data.
 # Then calculates the accuracy, precision, and recall of the model.

SVC_classifier = SVC()

SVC_classifier.fit(train_data, train_targets)

SVC_targets_predicted = SVC_classifier.predict(test_data)

SVC_accuracy = metrics.accuracy_score(test_targets, SVC_targets_predicted)

 # Prints the results of the 3 different models to be compared with eachother.
print(f"Training homes: {len(train_targets)}")
print(f"Test homes: {len(test_targets)}")

print()

print("| --- RandomForestClassifier --- |")
print(f"Accuracy: {RFC_accuracy:.2%}")

print()

print("| --- GaussianNB --- |")
print(f"Accuracy: {GNB_accuracy:.2%}")

print("")

print("| --- SVC --- |")
print(f"Accuracy: {SVC_accuracy:.2%}")
```

## QUESTION 2

1. For each model (your original one, and the 2 new ones for this task), display the classification report and the permutation importances for the most important features.  Discuss which model you would recommend to the Client and why.

I would reccomend the RandomForestClassifier since it is relatively fast and quite accurate especially when it is compared to the other two models. For example, for this question, I needed to import a pipeline and scaler for the SVC since it takes so much longer especially when itterating multiple times to graph the permutations. (This pipeline and scaler also unintentionally made the SVC model more accurate than it was previously but still not better than the RandomForestClassifier)

```{python}
 # Include and execute your code here
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

homes = pl.read_csv("dwellings_ml.csv")

predictors = ["stories", "numbaths", "livearea", "basement", "quality_C", "gartype_Att"]

features = homes.select(predictors).to_numpy()
targets = homes["before1980"].to_numpy()

train_data, test_data, train_targets, test_targets = train_test_split(features, targets, test_size = .3)

# Uses the same RandomForestClassifier model as before on the data.
RFC_classifier = RandomForestClassifier()
RFC_classifier.fit(train_data, train_targets)
RFC_targets_predicted = RFC_classifier.predict(test_data)

# Creates the classification report for the RFC model.
RFC_report = classification_report(test_targets, RFC_targets_predicted)

# Creates the chart for the most important classifiers for the RFC model.
RFC_permutation_results = permutation_importance(
  RFC_classifier,
  test_data,
  test_targets,
  scoring = "accuracy",
  n_repeats = 10,
  random_state = 42,
  n_jobs = 1
)

RFC_importance_df = (pl
  .DataFrame({
    "feature": predictors,
    "importance_pp": RFC_permutation_results.importances_mean * 100,
    "std_pp": RFC_permutation_results.importances_std * 100
  })
  .with_columns(
    (pl.col("importance_pp") - pl.col("std_pp")).alias("lower"),
    (pl.col("importance_pp") - pl.col("std_pp")).alias("upper")
  )
  .sort("importance_pp", descending=True)
)

RFC_importance_graph = (
  ggplot(
    RFC_importance_df.to_dict(as_series=False), 
    aes(
      x = "feature",
      y = "importance_pp"
    )
  ) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity", 
    fill="#2878A0"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "RFC Permutation",
    subtitle = " ",
    x = " ",
    y = "Decrease in accuracy (% points)"
  )
)

# Uses the GaussianNB model on the same data.
GNB_classifier = GaussianNB()
GNB_classifier.fit(train_data, train_targets)
GNB_targets_predicted = GNB_classifier.predict(test_data)

# Creates the classification report for the GNB model.
GNB_report = classification_report(test_targets, GNB_targets_predicted)

# Creates the chart for the most important classifiers for the GNB model.
GNB_permutation_results = permutation_importance(
  GNB_classifier,
  test_data,
  test_targets,
  scoring = "accuracy",
  n_repeats = 10,
  random_state = 42,
  n_jobs = 1
)

GNB_importance_df = (pl
  .DataFrame({
    "feature": predictors,
    "importance_pp": GNB_permutation_results.importances_mean * 100,
    "std_pp": GNB_permutation_results.importances_std * 100
  })
  .with_columns(
    (pl.col("importance_pp") - pl.col("std_pp")).alias("lower"),
    (pl.col("importance_pp") - pl.col("std_pp")).alias("upper")
  )
  .sort("importance_pp", descending=True)
)

GNB_importance_graph = (
  ggplot(
    GNB_importance_df.to_dict(as_series=False), 
    aes(
      x = "feature",
      y = "importance_pp"
    )
  ) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity", 
    fill="#2878A0"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "GNB Permutation",
    subtitle = "Averace accuracy decrease.",
    x = "Predictors",
    y = " "
  )
)

# Uses the SVC model on the same data. (Scaler is needed because SVC is so slow.)
SVC_classifier = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), SVC())
SVC_classifier.fit(train_data, train_targets)
SVC_targets_predicted = SVC_classifier.predict(test_data)

# Creates the classification report for the SVC model.
SVC_report = classification_report(test_targets, SVC_targets_predicted)

# Creates the chart for the most important classifiers for the SVC model.
SVC_permutation_results = permutation_importance(
  SVC_classifier,
  test_data,
  test_targets,
  scoring = "accuracy",
  n_repeats = 10,
  random_state = 42,
  n_jobs = 1
)

SVC_importance_df = (pl
  .DataFrame({
    "feature": predictors,
    "importance_pp": SVC_permutation_results.importances_mean * 100,
    "std_pp": SVC_permutation_results.importances_std * 100
  })
  .with_columns(
    (pl.col("importance_pp") - pl.col("std_pp")).alias("lower"),
    (pl.col("importance_pp") - pl.col("std_pp")).alias("upper")
  )
  .sort("importance_pp", descending=True)
)

SVC_importance_graph = (
  ggplot(
    SVC_importance_df.to_dict(as_series=False), 
    aes(
      x = "feature",
      y = "importance_pp"
    )
  ) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity", 
    fill="#2878A0"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "SVC Permutation",
    subtitle = " ",
    x = " ",
    y = " "
  )
)

# Displays the graphs and tables for each classifier.
print("| --- RandomForestClassifier --- |")
print(RFC_report)

print()

print("| --- GaussianNB --- |")
print(GNB_report)

print("")

print("| --- SVC --- |")
print(SVC_report)

display(gggrid([RFC_importance_graph, GNB_importance_graph, SVC_importance_graph]), ncol = 3)
```
